column2: cor(data_sgr$SGR_2m, data_sgr$mass, use="complete.obs") #-0.146; weak negative correlation between SGR and mass, let's look at temp-specific trends
#This tells us that correlation is stronger between SGR and mass at 18C than at 23C. Let's see if it is significant:
lm(formula = SGR_2m ~ mass * Temp, data = data_sgr)
#this shows a significant mass effect on SGR at both 18C treatments, and a near-significant mass effect on SGR at 23C. While the correlation is weak, it could mask our results.
data_sgr$SGR_2m_resid <- resid(lm(SGR_2m ~ log10(mass)*factor(Temp), data_sgr)) #residuals of SGR are also a good option for more effectively mass-standardizing my growth  measurements.
#note that there cannot be an individual level effect term in the above model as there is only one measurement per fish in the 18b dataset
ggplot(data = data_sgr, aes(x = mass, y = SGR_2m_resid, colour = factor(Temp), fill = factor(Temp))) +
